[[North Bethesda, Maryland|North Bethesda]], [[Maryland]] | former_school(s)= | awards = Big East's preseason player of the year 2007 }} '''Roy Denzil Hibbert''' (born [[December 11]], [[1986]]) is a collegiate men's [[basketball]] player in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]. He graduated from [[Georgetown University]]. ==Background== Roy Hibbert was born in [[Queens, New York|Queens]], [[New York]] to Roy, Sr. and Patty Hibbert. The family moved to [[Washington, District of Columbia|Washington]], [[District of Columbia|DC]] when Roy was 2. Around that time, the [[New York Post]] states that his parents introduced him to basketball after they had "tried to get him to play tennis, then golf, then the piano."[http://www.nypost.com/seven/03112007/sports/biggest_big_man_sports_lenn_robbins.htm?page=0 BIGGEST BIG MAN - New York Post] Hibbert attended [[Georgetown Preparatory School|Georgetown Prep]] in [[North Bethesda, Maryland|North Bethesda]], [[Maryland]]. The team was coached by Dwayne Bryant, who had attended [[Georgetown University]] as a varsity basketball player. Bryant introduced the still-awkward Hibbert to the GU campus.[http://hoyanews.blogspot.com/2006/02/daily-orange-roy-hibbert-profile.html Hoya News: The Daily Orange - Roy Hibbert Profile] Hibbert helped make [[Georgetown Preparatory School|Georgetown Prep]]'s Little Hoyas co-champions of the [[Interstate Athletic Conference]] in [[2004]].[http://guhoyas.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hibbert_roy00.html Player Bio: Roy Hibbert :: Men's Basketball] Hibbert was successfully recruited by [[Georgetown University]] coach [[Craig Esherick]] in 2003. However, [[Craig Esherick|Esherick]] was fired before Hibbert arrived on campus ([[Craig Esherick|Esherick]]'s last season as coach went 13-15). [[John Thompson III]] was hired as the new coach. Hibbert joined the [[Hoyas]] as a "project," a player who had potential but was not yet ready for varsity. ==Key attributes== At 7'2" and 278 lbs., Hibbert plays center under Coach [[John Thompson III]]. He has evolved from a "project" to being [[NBA]]-quality.[http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/03/03/AR2007030301249.html Thomas Boswell - For the Hoyas' Hibbert, a Quantum Leap - washingtonpost.com] Hibbert's greatest asset is his size--few schools have a center of comparable height and strength. He is projected to be one of the next great shot-blockers in all of basketball--his shot-blocking ability has been a major strength for him since his freshman year, when he trailed only Rigoberto Sargeant and four others in blocked shots per 40 minutes in his class.[http://kenpom.com/blog/index.php/weblog/americas_most_active_player/ the kenpom.com blog] He leads the [[NCAA]] in Effective Field Goal Percentage at 71%, and is 2nd in True Shooting Percentage at 72%.[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Roy-Hibbert-585/ Draft Express Profile] His slow-and-steady approach to the game meshes well with Coach Thompson's [[Princeton offense]], which emphasizes control over explosiveness. The [[Georgetown University]] [[Hoyas]] in 2007 have held many opponents to their lowest-scoring games of the season. In addition, Roy Hibbert has excellent free throw percentage, a major plus, given the frequency with which he is fouled.[http://www.nbadraft.net/profiles/royhibbert.asp NBA Draft.net - Roy Hibbert profile] His tireless work ethic has brought him to the forefront of the [[NCAA]]'s best centers. Hibbert's main weakness is temperamental--he sometimes lacks the aggressiveness necessary to dominate inside. ==Honors== Hibbert was named to the All-Big East Second Team in 2006 along with teammate [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Jeff Green]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/print?id=2356272&type=story Four unanimous selections to all-Big East first team] March 6, 2006 In 2007, he and [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Green]] were unanimous selections to the All-Big East First Team, with [[Jeff Green (basketball)|Green]] earning Big East player of the year honors. The two led the Hoyas to victory in the 2007 Big East Conference Championship for the first time since 1989 against the [[Pittsburgh Panthers basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]; Hibbert contributed a double-double with 18 points and 11 rebounds. Before the 2007-2008 season he was named Big East's preseason player of the year.{{cite news |url= http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/preview?gameId=273140046 |date= [[November 10]], [[2007]] |title= William & Mary-Georgetown Preview |work= [[ESPN]] |accessdate= 2008-06-02}} He was also named a preseason All-American along with the likes of [[Tyler Hansbrough]], whose [[Tar Heels]] were upset by Hibbert's Hoyas in the Elite Eight of the 2007 NCAA Tournament. ==Professional prospects== Hibbert had repeatedly said that he plans to play all four years and graduate from Georgetown, continuing the tradition of graduating Hoya centers such as [[Patrick Ewing]], [[Alonzo Mourning]], and [[Dikembe Mutombo]]. However, his performance in helping to lead the Hoyas to the 2007 Final Four catapulted him into lottery pick status. Hibbert declared his eligibility for the [[2007 NBA Draft]], but did not sign with an agent.[http://www.thehoya.com/sports/042007/sports1.cfm Sports | The Hoya] On [[May 23]], [[2007]], Hibbert announced he would return to school for his senior season. Hibbert said of Georgetown, "My heart was here. ... I feel like I have unfinished business here."[http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/wire?section=ncb&id=2880367 ESPN - Georgetown's Green remains in draft, Hibbert to return to school - Men's College Basketball] In the summer of 2007, Hibbert was the starting center on the U. S. squad at the Pan-American Games. The team was coached by [[Jay Wright (coach)|Jay Wright]] of [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]]. Following the Hoyas' upset loss in the second round of the 2008 NCAA Tournament, Hibbert's collegiate career came to a close.
